column7: 2026-11-06: ISO duration work: user rule — days are the largest unit (no months/years, ambiguous); formatting first, parsing is a later step. My own choices in formatISO: zero -> PT0S, negatives get leading '-', sub-second as decimal seconds (PT0.5S), input rounded to whole ms.

2026-11-06: Rule from user (security reviewer Leo, after the old ReDoS advisory against ms): no regular expressions in any new parsing code on this branch. The ISO duration parse side must be hand-written (manual char scanning).

2026-11-06: parseCompound (my choices): hand-scanned, no regex, since ms had a ReDoS advisory (the no-regex rule from feat/iso-duration was scoped to that branch, so I followed it by choice, not by rule). Every component needs a unit; a single leading '-' negates the total; non-string, empty or >100 chars returns NaN instead of throwing. Not committed yet.

2026-11-06: parseCompound now uses one anchored regex (validate whole string) plus a global component regex to sum, input capped at 100 chars. User changed the earlier hand-scanned approach for this PR: reviewer Ana prefers an anchored, length-capped regex. The no-regex rule was only for feat/iso-duration.

2026-11-06: parseISO (my choices): hand-scanned, no regex; throws on invalid input (like formatISO); rejects Y/M-in-date/W, accepts optional +/- sign, ',' or '.' decimal only on seconds; units must be in order, no repeats; '-PT0S' -> 0. Not committed yet.
